section: Constitutional, statutory, executive, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies - definitions and how to distinguish them
subsections: Constitutional vs extra-constitutional status - spotting the odd one out

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a constitutional body from a statutory body?
o: A statutory body enjoys constitutional protection, whereas a constitutional body can be changed by an ordinary Act
A constitutional body is provided for by the Constitution, whereas a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament
A constitutional body is created by executive resolution, whereas a statutory body is created by the Constitution
Both constitutional and statutory bodies are created only by presidential orders
accepted.x: A constitutional body is provided for by the Constitution, including its composition, powers or independence. A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament and can be altered by amending that Act.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related institutional categories by identifying their source of creation.
accepted.sec: Constitutional bodies → Article  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (Body)
a. Election Commission
b. Finance Commission
c. Comptroller and Auditor General
 d. National Commission for Backward Classes

List-II (Article)
i. Article 148
ii. Article 280
iii. Article 324
iv. Article 338B
accepted.x: The Election Commission is under Article 324, the Finance Commission under Article 280, the CAG under Article 148 and the NCBC under Article 338B.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Article–body pair and eliminate codes that disturb the established matches.
accepted.sec: Constitutional bodies → Article  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Union Public Service Commission, State Public Service Commissions and Joint State Public Service Commission are dealt with under Articles 315 to 323.
2. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is provided for under Article 338.
3. The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is provided for under Article 338A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Articles 315–323 concern the public service commissions, Article 338 concerns the NCSC and Article 338A concerns the NCST.
accepted.tq: Use a grouped Article range and neighbouring constitutional provisions to test precise institutional identification.
accepted.sec: Constitutional bodies → Article  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. GST Council — Article 279A — 101st Amendment, 2016
2. Attorney General of India — Article 76
3. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities — Article 350B
4. Inter-State Council — Article 263
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The GST Council is under Article 279A, the Attorney General under Article 76, the Linguistic Minorities Officer under Article 350B and the Inter-State Council under Article 263.
accepted.tq: Check each Article–office pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Constitutional bodies → Article  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out on the basis of constitutional status?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
accepted.x: The NCBC, CAG and Finance Commission are constitutional bodies. NITI Aayog is an executive, non-statutory body created by Cabinet resolution.
accepted.tq: Spot the executive body placed among constitutional bodies; status, not subject matter, is the basis of grouping.
accepted.sec: Constitutional vs extra-constitutional status - spotting the odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263.
2. It was set up by a Presidential Order in 1990.
3. The Inter-State Commerce Commission is associated with Article 307.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Inter-State Council has constitutional status under Article 263 despite being established by a Presidential Order in 1990; Article 307 concerns the Inter-State Commerce Commission.
accepted.tq: Handle the apparent contradiction between constitutional status and the manner of establishment.
accepted.sec: Constitutional vs extra-constitutional status - spotting the odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its parent Act and administrative ministry or department?
o: National Green Tribunal — Environment Protection Act, 1986 — Ministry of Law and Justice
National Commission for Women — National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 — Ministry of Minority Affairs
National Human Rights Commission — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 — Ministry of Home Affairs
Press Council of India — Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 — Ministry of Culture
accepted.x: The NHRC was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs. The other options substitute the wrong parent Acts or ministries.
accepted.tq: Use the parent-Act and ministry pairing to detect a wrong institutional association.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (Body)
a. National Commission for Women
b. National Commission for Minorities
c. National Green Tribunal
d. UIDAI

List-II (Parent Act)
i. Aadhaar Act, 2016
ii. National Commission for Women Act, 1990

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: National Commission for Minorities — Ministry of Minority Affairs
National Human Rights Commission — Ministry of Home Affairs
National Commission for Women — Ministry of Women and Child Development
National Green Tribunal — Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
accepted.x: The National Green Tribunal is associated with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, not the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong ministry by comparing each statutory body with its subject-related department.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Central Board of Direct Taxes is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963 — Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963 — Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Income Tax Act, 1961 — Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
Finance Commission Act, 1951 — Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: The CBDT functions under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963 and is placed under the Department of Revenue in the Ministry of Finance.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the parent Act from the substantive tax law and identify the correct department.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Press Council of India was established under which Act and is associated with which ministry?
o: Cinematograph Act, 1952 — Ministry of Information and Broadcasting
Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 — Ministry of Culture
Press Council Act, 1978 — Ministry of Home Affairs
Press Council Act, 1978 — Ministry of Information and Broadcasting
accepted.x: The Press Council of India is governed by the Press Council Act, 1978 and is associated with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
accepted.tq: Pair the statutory parent Act with the ministry having the corresponding communication portfolio.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the National Human Rights Commission after the 2019 amendment, consider the following statements:
1. Its Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India or a former Supreme Court judge.
2. It has three human-rights members, of whom at least one must be a woman.
3. The term of office is three years or until the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements reflect the post-2019 position. Earlier, only a former CJI could chair the NHRC, there were two human-rights members and the term was five years.
accepted.tq: Test amendment-based changes by contrasting the current rule with the earlier arrangement.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition and tenure of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: A chairperson, a vice-chairperson and five members, each serving three years
A chairperson and six members, each serving three years or until 70 years of age
A chairperson and four members, each serving five years
A chairperson, two vice-chairpersons and five members, each serving six years
accepted.x: The NCM consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson and five members, with each serving a three-year term.
accepted.tq: Use composition and tenure together to distinguish similar commissions.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Minorities:
1. Five of its seven members, including the Chairperson, must belong to notified minorities.
2. It is governed by the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
3. Its Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members serve for three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The NCM Act was enacted in 1992, and five of the seven members, including the Chairperson, must be from notified minorities; the tenure is three years.
accepted.tq: Combine composition, parent legislation and tenure in a single institutional profile.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Central Bureau of Investigation is correct?
o: The CBI is itself a constitutional body created under Article 324.
The CBI is a statutory body established directly by the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
The CBI derives its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 and is associated with the Department of Personnel and Training.
The CBI derives its powers exclusively from the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
accepted.x: The CBI is non-statutory in itself and draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946. It is associated with the Department of Personnel and Training.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an organisation's operational source of power from its own constitutional or statutory status.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation is chosen by a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India or nominee, and the:
o: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: The CBI Director is selected by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India or a nominee, and the Leader of the Opposition.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct appointing or selection authority by separating it from nearby constitutional offices.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, the Central Bureau of Investigation generally requires which of the following?
o: Prior consent of the concerned State Government
Consent of the Supreme Court in every case
Approval of the Election Commission of India
accepted.x: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires the consent of the concerned State Government for exercising CBI powers in that State. Several States have withdrawn general consent.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority must consent when a central investigative agency operates within a State.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The origin of the Central Bureau of Investigation is associated with which committee and period?
accepted.x: The origin of the CBI is associated with the Santhanam Committee of 1962–63.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with the committee and period specifically linked to its origin.
accepted.sec: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the method of creation and nature of the body?

1. Planning Commission — Government resolution — Advisory body
2. National Development Council — Executive resolution — Executive coordinating body
3. NITI Aayog — Cabinet resolution — Think tank
4. Law Commission — Department of Legal Affairs notification — Advisory research body
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. These bodies are not created as constitutional bodies by the Constitution; they arise through resolutions or executive notifications and perform advisory or coordinating functions.
accepted.tq: Test creation mechanism and institutional nature together instead of treating all non-constitutional bodies alike.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Planning Commission was created by a Government resolution in:
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was created by a Government resolution in March 1950. The Advisory Planning Board associated with K.C. Neogi preceded it in 1946.
accepted.tq: Use the year and month to distinguish the Planning Commission from other resolution-based bodies.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Planning Commission is correct?
o: It was a constitutional body under Article 263.
It was chaired by the President and included all Chief Ministers as members.
It was a statutory body chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
It was an advisory body chaired by the Prime Minister, and the States were not represented in it.
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was an advisory body created by Government resolution, chaired by the Prime Minister; the States were not represented in its composition.
accepted.tq: Separate chairperson, nature and representation from the arrangements of the NDC and NITI Aayog.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Development Council:
1. It includes the Prime Minister, all Union Cabinet Ministers, all Chief Ministers and Union Territory Administrators.
2. All Union Cabinet Ministers became members of it from 1967.
3. It was created by an executive resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The NDC was created by executive resolution and includes the listed Union and State-level leadership, with all Union Cabinet Ministers included from 1967.
accepted.tq: Combine original creation, later composition and membership categories in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
o: It consists only of Union Cabinet Ministers and Governors of States.
It consists of the President, Vice-President and all Governors of States.
It consists of all Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, with the Prime Minister as Chairperson of NITI Aayog.
It consists of Members of Parliament nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.x: NITI Aayog is a think tank with the Prime Minister as Chairperson, and its Governing Council includes all Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct membership pattern by contrasting it with constitutional bodies and the former Planning Commission.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that the National Development Council should be given constitutional status under Article 263 and renamed as the:
accepted.x: The Sarkaria Commission recommended constitutional status for the NDC under Article 263 and proposed the name National Economic and Development Council.
accepted.tq: Match a commission recommendation with the precise proposed institutional name and Article.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Law Commission of India:
1. It is a constitutional body.
2. It is a quasi-judicial body that advises the President.
3. It is an advisory research body that makes recommendations to the Government.
4. It reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are false. The Law Commission is neither constitutional nor statutory nor quasi-judicial, and it advises the Government rather than the President; statements 3 and 4 are correct.
accepted.tq: Reject familiar but incorrect labels by distinguishing advisory research from constitutional and quasi-judicial functions.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Law Commission is constituted through a notification issued by the:
accepted.x: The Law Commission is constituted through a notification of the Department of Legal Affairs and is constituted every three years.
accepted.tq: Identify the issuing department rather than the broader ministry commonly associated with the subject.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 23rd Law Commission of India covers which period?
accepted.x: The 23rd Law Commission operates from 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2027.
accepted.tq: Read both the starting and ending dates carefully; close periods are used as distractors.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who chaired the first Law Commission of India constituted in 1834?
accepted.x: The first Law Commission, constituted in 1834, was chaired by Lord Macaulay.
accepted.tq: Associate the earliest commission with its chairperson and distinguish it from the first post-Independence commission.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first Law Commission constituted after Independence in 1955 was chaired by:
accepted.x: The first Law Commission after Independence was constituted in 1955 under the chairmanship of M.C. Setalvad.
accepted.tq: Use the qualifying phrase ‘after Independence’ to avoid confusing two different first commissions.
accepted.sec: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)
